seoTitle: How to Fix Instagram's Unlike Problem (Likes Not Registering) 2026
metaDescription: Instagram like disappearing right after you tap it? Here's how to fix the unlike bug by checking your connection and updating the app, step by step.
intro: It's a small but maddening glitch: you tap the heart on a post, it fills in, and a second later it's back to outline — as if you never liked it at all. Instagram calls this an app-level sync issue rather than an account problem, which is good news, because it means the fix lives entirely on your phone. This guide covers the two things actually worth checking before you assume something is wrong with your account: your connection and your app version. Both take under two minutes and resolve the vast majority of reported cases.

steps.heading: Understand what the unlike bug actually looks like
steps.body: The symptom is consistent across reports: you double-tap or tap the heart icon under a post, the like registers for a moment — the icon fills red and the count ticks up — then it silently reverts to unliked without you touching anything. It happens most on Reels and video posts, where the like button sits in the same bottom-left cluster alongside the comment and share icons you see on any post in your feed. Because the action visually completes before reverting, it's easy to think you imagined tapping it at all, but the behavior is reproducible and has nothing to do with the specific post or account you're interacting with.

image.caption: A typical Instagram feed post, with the heart, comment, and share icons in the row where the unlike glitch shows up.

steps.heading: Check your internet connection first
steps.body: The most common cause is a weak or unstable connection dropping the like request after Instagram's app has already shown it as successful locally. If you're on mobile data in an area with poor signal, or on Wi-Fi that's dropping packets, switch networks and try liking the same post again. A quick way to confirm it's connection-related: turn on airplane mode, wait a few seconds, turn it back off, and reconnect before opening Instagram fresh rather than resuming a session that started on a bad connection.

steps.heading: Force close and reopen Instagram
steps.body: Before touching app store settings, fully close Instagram from your recent apps (don't just background it) and relaunch it. This clears out any stuck local state from the failed like request and is often enough on its own if the connection wasn't actually the problem. Give the app a few seconds to fully reload your feed before testing a like again, since testing mid-load can produce the same false-positive-then-revert behavior.

steps.heading: Update Instagram from the App Store or Play Store
steps.body: If the problem persists after confirming your connection is solid, the next step is making sure you're not running an outdated build. Exit Instagram, open the Google Play Store on Android or the App Store on iPhone, search for Instagram, and open its listing page. If the button reads Update instead of Open, your version is behind — tap Update and let it finish installing completely before relaunching the app. Outdated versions are a frequent cause of sync glitches like this one because Instagram ships frequent backend-compatible fixes that only take effect once the client is current.

steps.heading: Log out and back in if the issue continues
steps.body: When updating doesn't clear it, a full sign-out and sign-in resets your session token and forces the app to re-sync your account state from scratch, which fixes cases where the bug is tied to a corrupted local cache rather than the app version. Go to your profile, open the menu, and log out completely rather than just switching accounts if you use more than one. Log back in, let the feed load fully, and test liking a post you haven't interacted with recently.

image.caption: An Instagram profile page — the screen you'll use to sign out completely if the fix above doesn't clear the glitch.

steps.heading: Reinstall as a last resort
steps.body: If none of the above works, delete the app entirely and reinstall it fresh from the store rather than just updating. This clears every cached file the update process might have left behind and effectively gives you a clean install. You'll need to log back in afterward, but your likes, follows, and posts are all stored server-side, so nothing about your account or history is lost by removing and reinstalling the app.

faq.question: Why does my Instagram like disappear right after I tap it?
faq.answer: It's almost always a sync issue between the app and Instagram's servers, usually triggered by an unstable connection or an outdated app version — not a problem with your account or the post itself.

faq.question: Does this unlike bug affect all posts or just certain ones?
faq.answer: It's most commonly reported on Reels and video posts, but it can happen on any post type when the underlying cause is a connection drop or outdated app build.

faq.question: Will updating the Instagram app delete my saved posts or followers?
faq.answer: No. Updating, and even fully reinstalling the app, does not affect your account data — likes, follows, saved posts, and messages are stored on Instagram's servers, not on your device.

faq.question: I'm on the latest version and still have the problem — what else can I try?
faq.answer: Log out and back in to force a full session refresh, and if that fails, uninstall and reinstall the app for a completely clean state. If it still persists after that, it's worth checking Instagram's own help center for a wider outage affecting likes.

faq.question: Is the unlike glitch the same as the 'Try Again Later' error?
faq.answer: No — 'Try Again Later' is usually a temporary rate-limit or server-side block on an action, while the unlike glitch is a like that appears to succeed and then silently reverts. They can share the same fixes, but they're different symptoms.
